labels.label: theo:geroch
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial; nothing is presented as an anchor of the printed statement. THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IS VALID AGAINST THE PAPER'S NOTIONS AS RULED. (1) chronoMinkowski n is a topological spacetime in the paper's sense. defi:categorie_C/defi:causalite (l.232-252) ask only: a preorder, an open transitive relation contained in it, monotone in U. There is no closedness axiom and no standing assumption anywhere in ETT.tex except the openness of the chronological relation (l.243). The sheaf condition is met in its strongest form: chronoMinkowski is absolutely minimal (reflChrono_causallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimal), so it is no artefact of the missing gluing axiom (kb/0014). The paper itself builds Galileo's spacetime by the same rule, x <=_U y iff x << y or x = y (ex:causalities_lines item 4, l.274-276). R^{1,n} is second countable, Hausdorff, metrizable and locally compact. (2) The library predicates used are the paper's transcriptions. Tarentin is l.677. StronglyCausal is l.662 under DEC-7, and StronglyCausalOpen is proved too, which covers the 'open' reading of l.1215-1216. CausallyArcConnected is l.403 with DEC-6 curves. AdmissiblePast/Future are defi:mesure_dieckmann 1-4, with 4 for the outer measure (rem:mesure_bord) and K as defi:futur_continue, checked against l.761. IsCauchySurface is DEC-14 on the image, Inextensible is DEC-11/13, (ii) is DEC-10/12/15, and GloballyHyperbolic is l.995. Every curve notion is that of chronoMinkowski's own relation. (3) The key facts, checked by hand. << is Minkowski's, hence open. <= = (= or <<) is a preorder. Tarentin: x lies in I+(x - eps e0) cap I-(x + eps e0), which is inside the diamond. The causal curves are exactly the curves along which distinct points are <<-related locally. Strong causality is inherited, because J_refl(a,b) is a subset of J_Mink(a,b). Measures: I^-(q) minus J^-_Mink(p) is open and non-empty for p << q. J^-_refl(A) minus K^-_refl(A) lies in J^-_Mink(A) minus I^-(A), which lies in the boundary of I^-(A), an achronal Lipschitz graph and so Lebesgue-null. Cauchy surface: along a chronoMinkowski causal curve, t is non-decreasing. A limit P at a finite-time end satisfies c(s) << P, by Minkowski push-up (c(s) << c(s'') <=_Mink P). So the curve extends, and every inextensible curve has t running from -infinity to +infinity and meets {t=0} in exactly one point of its image. Diamonds: J((0,x),(2L,x)) is {vertices} union I+ cap I-, and the null-boundary point (L,y0) is a limit of points (L,g s) of the diamond, so the diamond is not closed and not compact. (4) Lean checks. GerochIIIImpIAsPrinted is literally the scaffold statement: a probe inhabits it with Causality.geroch_iii_imp_i, and derives False from not_geroch_tfae applied to Causality.geroch. The universe-0 instance suffices, because the scaffold theorems are universe-polymorphic. Paper line references 142-146, 1256-1267 and 1301-1306 were verified. The finding is TRUE: (iii)=>(i) and (ii)=>(i) fail as printed, and 'carries over verbatim' (l.1304-1306) is false. REPAIRED FORM. '<= closed' is a genuine strengthening: chronoMinkowski violates it, since its J+(p) = {p} union I+(p) is not closed. It is satisfiable: the timelike line is globally hyperbolic, so its <= is closed (probe: timelikeLine_globallyHyperbolic.isClosed_le timelikeLine_tarentin), and it has a Cauchy surface. GH + tarentin => <= closed is GloballyHyperbolic.isClosed_le, i.e. prop:GH_Jferme. The reduction around the sorry is correct. J(p,q) is closed. Each x has sigma in S with x <= sigma or sigma <= x (exists_le_or_le_of_isClosed_le, sorry-free), so J(p,q) lies in (J-(q) cap J+(S)) union (J+(p) cap J-(S)). The second piece is the dual of the first, and a closed subset of a compact set is compact. The sorry is the singleton, time-dual case of O'Neill's compactness lemma, under all of theo:geroch's hypotheses plus <= closed. Whether it holds in this topological generality is not established (minor finding 1).

labels.notes: Unmarked, partial, no reading taken, no edit to CausalScaffold.SingularGeroch. not_geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal quantifies exactly the signature of SingularFlatAxioms.geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal (universe 0), and a probe derived False from it. chronoMinkowski_singularFlatAxioms with sing = empty discharges every field. The BTZ fields are vacuous. The others are push-up, absolute minimality, causal arc-connectedness, tarentin, Z+ = M, Z- = M, T2, second countability, metrizability, local compactness, no isolated points, closed singular locus and empty interior. ModelMeasures uses M itself as the causally convex chart. FINDING CHECKED, TRUE AND CORRECTLY SCOPED. The library abstraction is refuted, not the paper: a genuine E_{>=0}-manifold with empty singular locus is a flat Lorentzian 3-manifold with null curves, not chronoMinkowski. lem:densite_modele (l.1464-1473) gives J+-(p) = closure(I+-(p)) in causally convex subsets of the models, a fact SingularFlatAxioms does not carry. The proof (l.1781, 'a direct consequence of Theorem theo:geroch') inherits the gap. The REPORT is right that a global-closedness repair would not apply there before (i) is known.

findings.where: scaffold/CausalScaffold/GerochCauchy.lean:47-50, 69-71, 771-773, 795; REPORT theo:geroch questions[0] ('Only the classical lemma J- (q) cap J+(S) compact remains unproved'), notes 2
findings.what: The repaired step is presented as resting on 'the classical lemma' alone, and the SCOPE says 'its sorry is O'Neill's quasi-limit argument'. The lemma (O'Neill's compactness of J-(q) cap J+(S) for a Cauchy surface S) is classical for Lorentzian manifolds, and the sorry adds '<= closed' to theo:geroch's hypotheses. Nothing shows it holds in this topological generality. The paper's own 'carries over verbatim' has just been refuted, and the sorry's obstruction text concedes that the library's substitute also needs J+-(S) closed and J- of open sets open, neither derived here. The usual route needs more than global closedness. It needs J-(S) minus S to be open, or J+(S) to be closed, to push the approximating curves across S, and the analogous results for Lorentzian length spaces assume local causal closedness and localizability. So geroch_of_isClosed_le is a conjecture, and the author should not adopt the '<= closed' repair on the strength of this REPORT. The Lean is honest: a tagged sorry, unmarked, status partial, called 'a reading'. Only the framing overstates.
findings.fix: Call the sorry 'the analogue, under these hypotheses, of O'Neill's compactness lemma, not known to hold in this generality' (docstring l.771-773 and l.795, SCOPE l.69-71, REPORT notes 2). Phrase the question to the author as: 'the repaired form is conjectural; is global closedness of <= the intended repair, or local causal closedness (alternative (a)), with the remaining lemma to be proved?'

findings.where: scaffold/CausalScaffold/GerochCauchy.lean:45-46; REPORT theo:geroch hypotheses[5] and questions[0]; scaffold/CausalScaffold/LimitCurves.lean:29, 293; REPORT kb_proposals[2]
findings.what: Two wording points. (1) 'which (i) implies (GloballyHyperbolic.isClosed_le, prop:relation_fermee)'. The implication 'tarentin + globally hyperbolic => <= closed' is prop:GH_Jferme (ETT.tex:1178), which is what GloballyHyperbolic.isClosed_le carries. prop:relation_fermee alone asks J+-(x) closed, which only the first half of prop:GH_Jferme supplies. (2) 'A closed causal relation gives a time function' (LimitCurves l.29, and the docstring at l.293). What is proved is a continuous function strictly increasing along <= (exists_strict_continuous_of_isClosed_le). Under DEC-10/DEC-12 a time function is a strong morphism, an open map inducing a sheaf morphism to the timelike line, and that is not proved. The declaration statements are correct; only the prose overstates.
findings.fix: Cite prop:GH_Jferme (with prop:relation_fermee as its ingredient). Replace 'time function' with 'continuous function strictly increasing along <=' in LimitCurves l.29, the docstring of exists_strict_continuous_of_isClosed_le, and kb_proposals[2].
